content: {"argument": "The change modifies the WWW-stripping regex to allow TLDs of 1–63 characters instead of 2–63, which aligns with RFC standards permitting single-character labels. The test expects preservation of 'www.' for single-character TLDs, but this behavior was never guaranteed—the prior regex incorrectly restricted TLD length. The updated regex correctly strips 'www.' from hostnames like 'www.example.a', producing 'http://example.a', which is valid and intended.", "concedes": false}
